titulo: Revisão Sistemática de Estudos Observacionais sobre o uso de Erlotinibe e Gefitinibe no Tratamento do Câncer de Pulmão de Células Não Pequenas
titulo_curto: Do targeted lung cancer drugs work outside trials? What the real world shows

autores.afiliacao: Merck Sharp & Dohme · Belo Horizonte, Brazil
São Paulo State University (Unesp) · Botucatu, Brazil
Brazilian National Cancer Institute (INCA) · corresponding author

em_1_minuto.titulo: Do they work in everyday hospital practice?
em_1_minuto.texto: Gefitinib and erlotinib were added to SUS, Brazil's public health system, in 2013 for a type of lung cancer with a mutation in the EGFR gene. Since then, no one had gathered data on their real-world use.
They searched for observational studies from 2014 to 2023. Of the 9,765 publications found, 8 studies made it into the final analysis.

em_1_minuto.titulo: More time without the disease progressing
em_1_minuto.texto: The targeted drugs gave longer survival and more time without progression than chemotherapy, with few adverse effects and adherence above 85%.

em_1_minuto.titulo: Monitoring what is already in SUS
em_1_minuto.texto: Assessing technologies after they enter the health system shows whether the promised benefit holds up in patients' real lives.

secoes.lede: The deadliest cancer in the world gained treatments that target a specific tumor mutation.

blocos.html:
Lung cancer is the deadliest (18.7% of cancer deaths) and the most frequent (12.4% of cases) cancer in the world. In Brazil, the estimate for each year from 2023 to 2025 was 18,020 cases in men and 14,540 in women. The most common type is non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), almost always found at an advanced stage.

The EGFR gene makes a receptor that controls the growth of the cells lining the tissues. When it mutates, the cell gets a nonstop “grow” signal. This mutation appears in about 30% of metastatic NSCLC. Gefitinib and erlotinib block this receptor: they are tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs).

itens: 2006 · Anvisa, Brazil's health regulator, registers erlotinib
2010 · Gefitinib becomes the first targeted therapy approved in Brazil for this cancer
2013 · Conitec adds both drugs to SUS
2024 · This review gathers real-world usage data for the first time

itens.texto: Controlled conditions and selected patients. It shows whether the drug works in the ideal setting.
Follows everyday use, with all kinds of patients. It shows whether the benefit holds up in practice.

secoes.lede: The question: do patients treated in everyday practice get the same results seen in clinical trials?

itens.texto: The review plan was registered in PROSPERO (CRD42022337969) before it started.
Adults with advanced or metastatic NSCLC with an activating EGFR mutation, treated for the first time with gefitinib or erlotinib alone, compared with chemotherapy, placebo or supportive care.
MEDLINE, EMBASE, Cochrane, LILACS, CINAHL, the Brazilian Digital Library of Theses and Dissertations and the Capes Journal Portal, from January 2014 to March 2023, in Portuguese, English and Spanish.
Two reviewers chose the studies and extracted the data independently; a third resolved disagreements. Of the 9,765 publications, 48 were read in full and 8 studies were included in the analysis.
Risk of bias was assessed with the Joanna Briggs Institute checklists. The planned meta-analysis was not possible, because the studies were too different from one another.

blocos.html: The 8 studies (6 prospective and 2 retrospective cohorts, from 2015 to 2020) came from the Czech Republic, Taiwan, Germany, China, the US and the Netherlands, with samples of 62 to 38,100 people. Gefitinib predominated, with just over 6,200 participants.

secoes.lede: Choose a result: survival, treatment adherence or symptom improvement.

parametros.leitura: In the largest study, done in Taiwan with more than 15,000 patients, those who took gefitinib or erlotinib lived a median of 6 to 8 months longer than those who had platinum chemotherapy.
In the two erlotinib studies, the vast majority of patients took the drug as prescribed. In the US study, 14.3% were not adherent.
In the only quality-of-life study (Taiwan), improvement in disease symptoms was greater and longer-lasting with gefitinib.

blocos.nota: Overall survival: study by Chung et al. (2019), with 5,638 patients on gefitinib, 1,433 on erlotinib and 8,703 on chemotherapy. Adherence: percentage of adherent patients. Symptoms: percentage of patients who improved.

itens.texto: In 3 of the 4 studies that measured it, gefitinib or erlotinib were better. The exception was a very small study (11 × 23 patients).
In 3 of 5 studies, the targeted drugs were better. In a German study, chemotherapy had a slight edge (18.1 × 17.4 months).
They were infrequent. The most common were diarrhea and skin rash, because the drug also acts on healthy lining tissues.

blocos.html: The mutation makes all the difference. In a Chinese study, patients with an EGFR mutation lived a median of 19 months on gefitinib; those without the mutation, only 7 months, less than with docetaxel chemotherapy (10 months). That is why testing for the mutation before treatment is essential.

secoes.titulo: Real world × the studies that led to SUS
secoes.lede: The authors compared the real-world results with those of the clinical trials used in the 2013 decision.

itens.texto: With gefitinib, the trials showed 9.2 to 10.8 months; in the real world, 9.6 to 11.0 months. With chemotherapy, 4.9 to 8.7 months.

itens.titulo: Overall survival: lower than in the trials
itens.texto: The trial at the time showed 30.5 months with gefitinib. In the real world, 19.0 to 19.6 months: much less, but still better than standard chemotherapy.
The only real-world study that measured time without progression on erlotinib found 12.2 × 5.6 months, a result similar to the trials.

blocos.titulo: Limitations pointed out by the authors
itens: The studies were very different from one another, which prevented a meta-analysis.
There were few events, which makes the estimates imprecise.
Observational studies have confounding factors, and all those included had some type of bias.
No studies with Brazilian patients were found.

secoes.titulo: What the study allows us to say
secoes.lede: The benefit exists in the real world, and monitoring technologies already incorporated is essential.

blocos.html:
Real-world data confirm the benefit of gefitinib and erlotinib in time without disease progression, but not the same gain in overall survival seen in the trials. Adverse effects were infrequent, adherence was high and there was a prolonged improvement in quality of life, especially with gefitinib.

Since Conitec decided on incorporation in 2013 with still-partial data, the authors stress the importance of monitoring technologies after they enter SUS.

glossario.def: Non-small cell lung cancer: the most common type of lung cancer.
Receptor that controls cell growth. When the gene mutates, it drives the tumor.
A change in the gene that leaves the receptor “switched on” all the time.
Targeted drug that blocks the growth signal sent by EGFR.
Two TKIs taken as pills, used in NSCLC with an EGFR mutation.
Treatment with cisplatin or carboplatin, the standard before targeted drugs.
Time the patient lives without the disease progressing.
The middle value: half of the patients were above it and half below.
A study that follows patients treated in everyday practice, without random assignment of treatment.
How closely the patient follows the treatment as prescribed.
Data obtained outside clinical trials, in everyday health care practice.
Ministry of Health committee that assesses whether technologies should enter SUS, Brazil's public health system.
International registry where researchers publish the plan of a review before carrying it out.
